fig:soft: Depletion of a soil at suction $h$ (0 at field capacity, 1 at the wilting point): $f(h)=\dfrac{S_e(100)-S_e(h)}{S_e(100)-S_e(15\,849)}$, with $S_e(h)=[1+(\alpha h)^n]^{-(1-1/n)}$; 100\,cm is field capacity and 15\,849\,cm ($pF=4.2$) the wilting point.

Critical suction of a soil for the common depletion $f^*=0.45$: $S_e^*=S_e(100)-f^*[S_e(100)-S_e(15\,849)]$, then $h^*=\alpha^{-1}\bigl[(S_e^*)^{-1/m}-1\bigr]^{1/n}$, $m=1-1/n$. For coarse loam this gives 387\,cm, the number in the sensor box.
The trigger of a soil for depletion $f_t$ is found the same way with $f_t$ in place of $f^*$ (471\,cm for $f_t=0.50$); the program solves $f(h)=f_t$ by bisection on $\log_{10}h$.
Readily available water: $\mathrm{RAW}=f_t\cdot\mathrm{TAW}$, with $\mathrm{TAW}$ the available water of the root zone (144\,mm here).
Days from field capacity to the trigger: $t=f_t\,\mathrm{TAW}/ET_c$; for coarse loam $0.50\times144/3.4\approx21$\,days, as written in the diagnosis.
The reach of the article decides whether the trigger can ever be read: if $h_t>h_c$ (\cref{eq:s-hc}) the crop cannot dry the soil to the trigger and the trigger is blind.

Field capacity and wilting point of each cell from its sand $S$, clay $C$ and organic matter $OM$ (fractions, SoilGrids 2.0, 0--60\,cm) by the regressions of Saxton and Rawls (2006): $\theta_{33}$ and $\theta_{1500}$.
Slope of the retention curve: $\lambda=\dfrac{\ln1500-\ln33}{\ln\theta_{33}-\ln\theta_{1500}}$; for $\psi\ge33$\,kPa, $\theta(\psi)=\theta_{33}\,(\psi/33)^{-\lambda}$.
Available water $AW=\theta_{33}-\theta_{1500}$, and the trigger water content $\theta_t=\theta_{33}-f\,(\theta_{33}-\theta_{1500})$.
Matric potential now, the inverse of the curve: $\psi=33\,(\theta/\theta_{33})^{-1/\lambda}$\,kPa, with $\theta$ the water content of the cell from the water balance (or from sensors when installed).

Days to the trigger: $t=\max\bigl(0,\,(\theta-\theta_t)\,z_r\cdot10/ET_c\bigr)$ with $z_r$ in cm and $ET_c$ in mm/day. With $AW=0.112$, $f=0.5$, $z_r=15$\,cm, $ET_c=0.8$: at field capacity $t=0.5\times0.112\times150/0.8=10.5$\,days; the mean 6.7 days is shorter because the cells are already below field capacity.
Units: 1\,kPa $\approx$ 10.2\,cm of water, so 33\,kPa $\approx$ 337\,cm and 1\,500\,kPa $\approx$ 15\,300\,cm, the same limits as the suction scale of the article.
Number of Daisy runs of an experiment with factors of $n_1,n_2,\dots$ levels and a budget $B$: $N=\min\bigl(\prod_i n_i,\,B\bigr)$.
If $\prod_in_i>B$, a Latin hypercube of $B$ runs is drawn so that each level of factor $i$ is used $\lfloor N/n_i\rfloor$ or $\lceil N/n_i\rceil$ times.

Every run is one full Daisy simulation; its annual fluxes (transpiration, soil evaporation, drainage, irrigation, yield) are what the article compares between methods with the rainfed twin, $\eta_X=\sum(X-X_0)/\sum I$.
